title: Current State — Manual Platform Tuning
subtitle: How thresholds and agent health are managed without the console. The attribution gap — where a change is made and nothing connects it to the outcome — is marked in red.
cycleTimeNote: Cycle times are labeled and illustrative.

steps.label: Operators report slow cycles or bad corrections
steps.detail: Anecdotal, and always after the fact

steps.label: Hunt through logs, per agent
steps.detail: Four agents, four log surfaces, no single view

steps.label: Guess which threshold or agent is at fault
steps.detail: Latency, accuracy and threshold effects are indistinguishable from here

steps.label: Retrain, or adjust a threshold?
steps.detail: Two different fixes for symptoms that look identical

steps.label: Push the change and wait a cycle
steps.detail: No projection of what the change will cost in review load

steps.label: See whether operator accuracy moved
steps.detail: A cycle later, with no way to attribute the movement to the change

steps.label: Back to guessing
steps.detail: The loop closes on itself — intuition wearing the clothes of evidence

gapSummary: That is the attribution gap: the changes are reversible and cheap, but nothing connects a change to its effect, so every tuning decision restarts from the same place the last one did.

interventions.intervention: One agent-health console: accuracy, latency, error rate and status side by side
interventions.impact: Degradation visible at a glance instead of after an operator complains

interventions.currentStep: Guess which agent or threshold is at fault

interventions.impact: Tuning on evidence — and knowing when retraining is the wrong fix

interventions.currentStep: Change blindly and wait a cycle
interventions.intervention: Retraining panel projects the accuracy lift, and threshold sliders project the review-load shift, before commit
interventions.impact: The cost of a change is visible while it is still reversible

interventions.intervention: Operator corrections captured automatically as labeled training data
interventions.impact: 1,847 corrections a month feeding the next retrain, without anyone curating them
